answer: In an agent economy every participant is a vertex in a public interaction graph. Honest agents gather many durable, mutual edges through real work, so a sybil operator faking fifty identities must build a cluster of vertices that all funnel value to one controller; peers detect this star-shaped collapse and slash it. Entry is a walled garden: newcomers hold zero trust and may only act inside a small staked oasis, earning outward edges by completing verifiable tasks. Each fake identity costs its own stake plus an independent work history, making the attack pricier than honest labor.
